Hertz mène ses expériences de 1886 à 188: Hertz carried out his experiments from 1886 to 1889 in Karlsruhe and confirmed the waves predicted by Maxwell. Asked about applications, he replied: "Nothing, I guess." He died in 1894, aged 36; the unit of frequency bears his name.
En 1800, William Herschel place un therm: In 1800, William Herschel placed a thermometer beyond the red end of a spectrum of sunlight: it warmed up. A year later, Johann Ritter discovered on the other side, beyond violet, rays that darken silver chloride.
Le Français Paul Villard découvre les ra: Frenchman Paul Villard discovered gamma rays in 1900 while studying radium. Ernest Rutherford named them in 1903, and showed with Edward Andrade in 1914 that their wavelength is shorter than that of X-rays.
Percy Spencer n'avait pas fini l'école p: Percy Spencer had not finished grammar school and taught himself in the Navy. Others had seen a candy bar melt near a radar; he looked into it, popping corn and bursting an egg. The first commercial oven, in 1947, stood about 6 feet tall and weighed 750 pounds.
Le 8 novembre 1895, à Würzburg, Röntgen: On 8 November 1895, in Würzburg, Röntgen saw a screen glow near a discharge tube. He called the rays "X", the letter for the unknown. Six weeks later, he imaged the hand of his wife Anna Bertha, who exclaimed: "I have seen my death!"
Newton est le premier à employer le mot: Newton was the first to use the word "spectrum" in 1671 for light split by a prism; he first counted six colours and later added indigo. Thomas Young was the first to measure the wavelengths of colours, in 1802.
Le 12 décembre 1901, Marconi écoute à Si: On 12 December 1901, Marconi listened at Signal Hill, Newfoundland, with a kite-borne antenna, for a signal sent from Poldhu about 3,500 km away. No automatic record was made, and historians doubt he really received it. He shared the 1909 Nobel Prize with Ferdinand Braun.
En 1985, l'autorité américaine des téléc: In 1985, the US communications regulator opened the 2.4 GHz band to unlicensed use. NCR and AT&T created the precursor of Wi-Fi in 1991 in the Netherlands, for cash registers; the 802.11 standard came out in 1997. The name Wi-Fi was coined by a branding agency in 1999.
On croyait la lumière portée par un « ét: Light was thought to be carried by an "aether". In 1887, in Cleveland, Albert Michelson and Edward Morley tried to measure the aether wind and found nothing: it has been called the most famous failed experiment in history.
En 1801, Johann Ritter découvre au-delà: In 1801, Johann Ritter discovered invisible rays beyond violet that darken silver chloride; they were long called "chemical rays". Their effect on DNA was only established in 1960.
En janvier 1935, le ministère britanniqu: In January 1935, the British Air Ministry asked whether a "death ray" was possible. Arnold Wilkins calculated that it was not, but suggested locating aircraft by radio: on 26 February 1935, at Daventry, a bomber was detected. In 1956, Robert Watson-Watt was stopped for speeding by a radar gun.
Le 23 décembre 1947, Walter Brattain fai: On 23 December 1947, Walter Brattain demonstrated a germanium point-contact transistor that amplified speech. Julius Lilienfeld had filed a patent on the principle as early as 1925 in Canada, and Germans Mataré and Welker independently invented the "transistron" in 1948.
Karl Ferdinand Braun découvre en 1874 qu: Karl Ferdinand Braun discovered in 1874 that a contact between a metal and a mineral lets current through in one direction only. John Ambrose Fleming patented the first vacuum diode on 16 November 1904, and William Eccles coined the word "diode" in 1919, from the Greek for "two paths".
Henry Joseph Round, des laboratoires Mar: Henry Joseph Round, of the Marconi labs, saw a carborundum crystal emit light under voltage in 1906; Soviet inventor Oleg Losev built an LED in 1927. The first white LEDs went on sale in autumn 1996.
L'ancêtre du condensateur est la bouteil: The ancestor of the capacitor is the Leyden jar, discovered on 11 October 1745 by Ewald von Kleist and then by Musschenbroek in Leiden. Abbé Nollet sent its discharge through 180 royal guards before Louis XV, and Franklin spoke of an "electrical battery" in 1749.
William Shockley installe son laboratoir: William Shockley set up his laboratory in Mountain View in 1956 and preferred silicon to germanium. Journalist Don Hoefler popularised the phrase "Silicon Valley" on 11 January 1971, in the weekly Electronic News.
En 1833, Faraday remarque que le sulfure: In 1833, Faraday noticed that silver sulfide conducts better when heated, unlike metals. The word Halbleiter, "semiconductor", appeared in 1910 in Josef Weiss's thesis.
Nouvel employé de Texas Instruments, Jac: As a new Texas Instruments employee, Jack Kilby had no summer vacation in 1958: he spent it on the problem. On 12 September 1958, he showed his germanium circuit to management. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2000.
Le premier microprocesseur, l'Intel 4004: The first microprocessor, the Intel 4004, came out on 15 November 1971 with 2,300 transistors. It had been ordered by Japan's Busicom for its calculators.
L'ENIAC, construit à l'université de Pen: ENIAC, built at the University of Pennsylvania by John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert, was unveiled on 14 February 1946. It weighed 27 tonnes; several tubes burned out almost every day. Six women did most of its programming, long unrecognised.
Dès 1903, l'Allemand Albert Hanson décri: As early as 1903, German Albert Hanson described flat conductors laminated to an insulating board. Austrian Paul Eisler invented the printed circuit around 1936 for a radio set; the United States used it on a large scale around 1943 for proximity fuzes.
Willard Boyle et George Smith inventent: Willard Boyle and George Smith invented the CCD sensor in 1969 at Bell Labs, while looking for a new kind of memory. In 1975, Steven Sasson at Kodak built the first digital still camera from it, at 100 × 100 pixels. Boyle and Smith received the Nobel Prize in 2009.
Vers 1893, AEG en Allemagne choisit le 5: Around 1893, AEG in Germany chose 50 Hz and Westinghouse in the United States 60 Hz, hence the world's two frequencies today.
Pour discréditer l'alternatif, Harold Br: To discredit alternating current, Harold Brown electrocuted dogs in 1888 in public demonstrations, secretly linked to Edison's company. On 6 August 1890, the first electric chair execution, of William Kemmler, used alternating current: the first jolt did not kill him.
Faraday enroule dès 1831 deux bobines su: Faraday wound two coils on an iron ring as early as 1831. Lucien Gaulard and John Gibbs showed a transformer in London in 1882 and in Turin in 1884; in 1885, Ganz engineers in Budapest patented the closed core, the basis of today's transformers.
En 1890, la première ligne à haute tensi: In 1890, the first high-voltage alternating-current line linked Willamette Falls to Portland, Oregon. In 1891, the Lauffen-Frankfurt line ran about 175 km at 15,000 volts.
Héron d'Alexandrie décrit déjà une roue: Hero of Alexandria already described a wind-driven wheel, and the windmills of Sistan in Iran were turning from the 7th century. In July 1887, Scotsman James Blyth lit his holiday home with the first electric wind turbine.
Les cellules restent une curiosité jusqu: Cells remained a curiosity until 1954: Calvin Fuller, Daryl Chapin and Gerald Pearson presented the first practical cell at Bell Labs. The Vanguard I satellite carried some as early as 1958.
Après le choc pétrolier de 1973, le Prem: After the 1973 oil crisis, Prime Minister Pierre Messmer announced a vast nuclear programme on 6 March 1974. France built 56 reactors in fifteen years; the very first had been commissioned at Marcoule from 1956.
En 1878, à Cragside, en Angleterre, Will: In 1878, at Cragside in England, William Armstrong set up the first hydroelectric scheme, for a single arc lamp in his art gallery. Edison's first hydroelectric station started on 30 September 1882 in Appleton, Wisconsin.
Stanley Whittingham invente le principe: Stanley Whittingham invented the principle at Exxon in 1974, but metallic lithium caught fire; John Goodenough and Koichi Mizushima found a better cathode in 1980, and Akira Yoshino the anode in 1985. Sony sold the first batteries in 1991.
La première station de pompage date de 1: The first pumped-storage plant dates from 1907, in Switzerland, near Schaffhausen. In 2020, such plants accounted for about 95% of the world's electricity storage installations.
La centrale de Pearl Street, à Manhattan: Pearl Street Station, in Manhattan, started on 4 September 1882 and supplied 400 lamps for 82 customers, in direct current at 110 volts. It burned down in 1890 and ran until 1895.
Bien avant Leibniz, les trigrammes du Yi: Long before Leibniz, the trigrams of the Chinese I Ching (9th century BC) resemble binary numbers, and India's Pingala described metre with short and long syllables. Leibniz wrote his first text on binary in 1679.
Le mot byte est inventé en juin 1956 par: The word byte was coined in June 1956 by Werner Buchholz at IBM, for the Stretch computer: he respelled bite as byte so it would not be confused with bit. The word "octet" unambiguously means 8 bits.
George Boole, autodidacte qui enseigne d: George Boole, self-taught and teaching from age 16, published his algebraic logic in 1847 and then in The Laws of Thought in 1854. It is this algebra that Shannon applied to circuits.
Babbage décrit sa machine en 1837 et ne: Babbage described his machine in 1837 and did not finish it, for lack of money and after a conflict with his engineer. His son Henry built a small part that, in 1910, calculated a list of multiples of pi... a wrong one. In 1991, London's Science Museum built his Difference Engine No. 2, which works.
Le mot bug est bien plus ancien : Thomas: The word bug is much older: Thomas Edison used it in a letter of 13 November 1878 for an invention's little faults. The log book with the moth is kept at the National Museum of American History in Washington.
Gordon Moore l'écrit en 1965 dans la rev: Gordon Moore wrote it in 1965 in Electronics magazine, under the title "Cramming more components onto integrated circuits". Caltech professor Carver Mead later popularised the name "Moore's law". The pace has slowed since around 2010.
Le rapport de John von Neumann de 1945 s: John von Neumann's 1945 report built on the work of Eckert and Mauchly, but circulated under his name alone, which angered them. The first stored program ran on 21 June 1948, on the Manchester "Baby".
La première vraie mémoire vive est le tu: The first true random-access memory was the Williams tube, which ran the Manchester "Baby"'s first program on 21 June 1948. Robert Dennard invented the one-transistor cell at IBM in 1966, and Intel sold the first such chip in 1970.
Le mot bit, contraction de binary digit,: The word bit, short for binary digit, comes from a Bell Labs memo by John Tukey dated 9 January 1947. Claude Shannon took it up in his founding 1948 paper.
Conçu par l'ingénieur des postes Tommy F: Designed by Post Office engineer Tommy Flowers, Colossus broke the German Lorenz cipher: the first message fell on 5 February 1944, and the Mark 2 was ready on 1 June 1944, just before D-Day. After the war, Flowers was ordered to burn the plans.
Le mot « logiciel » est formé en 1969 pa: The word "logiciel" was formed in 1969 by the Délégation à l'informatique, in charge of the Plan Calcul, from "logique" and "matériel". The Académie française adopted it in 1972.
En 1937, Claude Shannon montre dans son: In 1937, Claude Shannon showed in his MIT master's thesis that Boolean algebra and binary arithmetic can drive relays and switches: the basis of digital circuits.
